tells: The typography is the subject: Latin and katakana letterforms are fragmented and constructed from modular parts, and the word TOKYO resolves out of glitch noise

Dense, layered frames: scanlines, dot-matrix pixel type, halftone grids, registration marks, paper-like print texture over the digital elements

tells: A specific, memorable conceit: clockwork cities unfold out of a map inside an astrolabe, so the world itself is the title sequence and only this piece could have it

Clear choreography: the camera moves between mechanisms and locations, and the opening and closing frames bookend on the sun-lit astrolabe band
Logo lock-up integrated into the sculpted band with dragons and lion, so title and object are one
gaps: Typography is classical and safe; it serves the piece but takes no risk in the way the 3D world does
The palette leans heavily on warm sepia and bloom; more cold contrast in the map and stone areas would add range
Credit placement is somewhat standard (lower third, small caps) next to the ambition of the image

No physical light or depth: everything stays on the screen plane, while B gives its world real material
Some frames (the dot-matrix frame especially) lose hierarchy in the noise; edit for clearer focal moments
